tasks.behavior: Payments confirm and settle without waiting for unrelated offered networks
acceptance: Reproduce: a payment final on its own network stays unbooked while another offered network lags. Keep a regression test.
The first payment final on its own network chooses its option, is booked and queued to settle at once; no other offered network is waited for.

notes: 2026-10-30 Owner request: investigate and fix cross-network waiting, then let the implementing agent merge. This task records findings only; no implementation is started.

2026-10-30 Root cause: internal/ledger/process.go:100-126 refuses to choose an option until every other enabled option chain has last_finalized_time greater than the deposit block_time. It returns before booking; settlement_intents are created only after paid at lines 336-343. The slowest offered network therefore delays faster ones.

2026-10-30 Current policy deliberately chooses the earliest payment across chains (R-119/D-76), protecting an earlier full payment from later dust. This is a policy change, not permission to delete the guard or replace finalized evidence with latest blocks. Preserve the safety purpose through an explicit attempt-selection design.

2026-10-30 internal/invoice/pick.go:16-18 currently treats the payer pick as display preference, not binding payment selection. internal/invoice/payments.go:61 labels detected as Confirming even when the deposit itself is confirmed and only cross-network selection is waiting.

Tempo 0x4735a3cc5987f8d264af525219ac6bdc5a3447eabfbe03597692f785f79f9448 detected in 3.8s, waited 1351.6s, then signed in 7.2s and settled in 10.0s from queue. The dominant delay was before signing.

Advance only the unrelated cursor and observe the current implementation finally queue settlement. Extend existing internal/ledger/options_test.go coverage; use disposable data.

tasks.behavior: A deposit below 1 USD never decides which option a payer-chooses invoice takes
acceptance: A final deposit below the minimum (1 USD, or the invoice amount if smaller) never chooses an option; the first payment at or above it, on any option, is chosen.
Money below the minimum stays held for the payer and stays refundable; it never blocks the invoice from expiring or from settling the chosen option.
Payer and owner pages show it as money held for the payer, never as a partial payment of an option nobody chose.
Tests: dust on one network before a full payment on another; a real partial payment then a top-up; dust only, then expiry.
R-56, R-119 and D-90 state the minimum, and PLAN's open dust-threshold item is closed.
